subject: Intermittent tenant quota throttling — API rate-limit errors and immediate mitigations
messages:
From: Luke Bradford <luke@brightaxis.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: API errors this morning — intermittent rate limit failures

Hi Monica,

We started seeing a spike of 429s from the Redwood API beginning ~08:45 PDT this morning. It affected multiple upstream ETL jobs that hit our tenant (tenant_id=tenant123). Samples: 
- 2027-08-22T08:50:12Z: POST /v1/generate -> HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests (x-request-id: rq_7f9a2)
- 2027-08-22T09:02:35Z: POST /v1/chat -> HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests (x-request-id: rq_7fb3e)

The errors started resolving intermittently around 09:30 but we still see periodic failures. This is blocking our morning batch and causing backfill issues. Can you confirm whether this is tenant-level throttling on your side or something in our integration?

Thanks,
Luke Bradford
Platform Engineering
BrightAxis

--
Attachment: recent-error-sample.txt (text)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: support@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-22T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: API errors this morning — intermittent rate limit failures

Team — FYI, forwarding BrightAxis's report. Luke is seeing repeated 429s for tenant123 during the morning window. Can we triage ASAP?

Immediate asks:
- Can infra confirm whether any recent config changes or deploys touched per-tenant quota policy for tenant123?
- Check routing: were requests temporarily routed to a cheaper model variant with stricter per-tenant caps?
- If this is config drift, what's the fastest rollback or temporary mitigation?

I've CC'd support for case creation. I will reply to BrightAxis with an initial acknowledgement and a short mitigation plan once we have an internal triage.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-22T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: API errors this morning — intermittent rate limit failures

Quick triage notes:
- I pulled telemetry for tenant123 between 08:30-09:40 PDT. Observed a sharp rise in average prompt length and token usage per request starting ~08:44. Sequence lengths jumped ~3x compared to baseline, likely due to a new batch that expanded context windows.
- Config audit shows a recent automated policy sync at 03:12 UTC that pushed a new per-tenant quota object. There appears to be a mismatch: the policy for tenant123 has a lower soft limit than intended (soft_limit: 120 rps, expected 800 rps).
- No evidence of infra-wide throttles; this looks like misapplied tenant quota.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Apply temporary soft_limit bump to 800 rps for tenant123 (manual override).
2) Enable per-tenant circuit breaker to route overflow to a reserved dedicated pool for BrightAxis if available.
3) Collect all request ids and hand off to SRE for log bundling (I started a bundle; attaching request-id-logs.zip).

If operations can confirm step 1 within ~30–45 minutes, we should see error dropoff.

-Neha
Senior Support Engineer
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-22T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: API errors this morning — intermittent rate limit failures

Status update and steps I executed: 
- Root cause: automated policy sync job incorrectly merged tenant123 into a low-capacity quota group (quota_group=small-std). The expected mapping was quota_group=enterprise-burst. The merge happened due to a key collision in the sync logic.
- Mitigation applied at 10:12 PDT: manual override of tenant123 quota -> soft_limit=800 rps, burst_window=5s.
- Pushed routing rule to allow fallback to dedicated pool da-dedicated-4 when queue depth > 20 for tenant123.
- Attached config diff: config-diff-tenant123.txt (shows before/after).

ETA for a durable fix: I will submit a patch to the sync job to de-duplicate keys and add a safety check; estimate 2 business days for testing and deploy. For immediate safety, I locked the sync job (paused) until we finish patching.

-Karthik
Principal SRE Engineer
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Luke Bradford <luke@brightaxis.com>, BrightAxis Engineering <support@brightaxis.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-22T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: API errors this morning — intermittent rate limit failures

Hi Luke — thanks for reporting and for the logs you attached. 

What we did (short version):
- Identified a misapplied quota policy for tenant123 that reduced the tenant soft limit during an automated sync.
- At 10:12 PDT we manually bumped your tenant soft limit to 800 rps and enabled a temporary fallback to our reserved Dedicated pool for overflow.
- Paused the offending sync job and started a patch to the sync logic to prevent key collisions (ETA: 2 business days for permanent fix).

Immediate impact: you should see a sharp reduction in 429s. Please verify on your side; our telemetry shows error rate drop from ~7% to <0.3% within 15 minutes of the mitigation.

Short-term recommendations for BrightAxis:
- Implement exponential backoff on 429s (start with base 200ms, cap at 2s) and jitter.
- Reduce batch concurrency where possible during peak runs.
- If you need higher headroom long-term, we can discuss reserving Dedicated capacity or an increased quota SLA.

Attached: runbook-temporary-limits.pdf (short mitigation steps and recommended client backoff), request-id-logs.zip (our collected logs for your reference), config-diff-tenant123.txt.

We will follow up with a written incident summary and a proposed timeline for the sync-job patch and additional safeguards.

Would you like a quick 30-minute call today to review the mitigation and discuss long-term options?

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Luke
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-26T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: API errors this morning — intermittent rate limit failures

Luke — following up with the promised post-incident notes and next steps:

Summary: automated quota sync introduced a key-collision that assigned tenant123 to a lower-capacity quota group. That misconfiguration reduced your soft_limit and produced intermittent 429s when your recent longer-context batch started.

What we changed:
- Manual override applied 2027-08-22T10:12 PDT (soft_limit=800 rps).
- Fallback routing to dedicated pool enabled.
- Sync job paused and patch submitted; engineering review complete and patch scheduled for 2027-08-27 for canary and 2027-08-29 for full rollout.

Billing impact: the temporary soft_limit bump is considered a safety remediation and will not be charged as an overage for August. We will confirm final billing adjustments in the upcoming invoice; no surprise charges.

Permanent mitigation plan:
- Add dedupe and schema validation to the quota sync job (Karthik owner).
- Add an automated guardrail to reject quota merges that decrease effective capacity by >50% without manual approval.
- Improve telemetry alerts to identify sudden per-tenant capacity drops within 5 minutes.

We appreciate the call earlier — I will share a public-friendly postmortem doc and the incident timeline by end of day tomorrow. If you'd like a written SLA addendum or to discuss Dedicated reservation options, happy to loop in Sales Ops.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
